Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. content.content:
### 1.3 Open

**D39 — every discovered group member browses, and none of them can be pulled.**
`NexusDetector` synthesises each member as `host + "/repository/" + name`
(`nexus.go:117`, `nexus.go:156`). Measured against `pic-nexus.spw.dev.wallonie.be`
on 2026-08-10:

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /repository/dhi-io-proxy/v2/eclipse-temurin/tags/list` | **200** — the browse works |
| `GET /v2/repository/dhi-io-proxy/eclipse-temurin/manifests/21` | **404** |

The second is the path the Docker client builds from that same URL: it puts
`/v2/` first and the whole repository path after it. So the tags table fills
correctly and `p` on any row of it cannot work — the one produces a reference the
other cannot resolve.

It is not a matter of picking a better format string. Which of the four
addressing forms applies is a per-repository Nexus setting, and on this instance
the endpoint carrying it answers 403; the evidence and the design are in
[§3.18](#318-a-registry-member-is-an-address-not-a-url--repo_prefix). Until then
a member row is honest about tags and silently wrong about pulls, which is the
worse half — nothing on screen says the reference will not resolve.

Not reached before now because discovery had never succeeded against a group here
(the same 403), so no member row had ever been rendered.

**D40 is fixed** — see §1.1. It was reachable on its own and was fixed on its
own; §3.18 is what would have made it the normal case rather than a way to
misconfigure, and it no longer has to carry that.

**D39 is the only one open**, above. D21 and D36 closed everything that preceded
them; both are in §1.1.

D12, D13 and D14 were all fixed by §3.8 — see "The three defects it closed"
there for what each turned out to be. D14's inverted test failed the moment the
fix landed, which is what the pattern is for, and has been turned around.

**D35 — the "unpulled" count is only as fresh as the last fetch. Mitigated by
§3.17, not closed.** `detectGitStatus` computes it with
`rev-list --count HEAD..@{u}` (`workspaces/entry.go:90`), and `@{u}` is the local
remote-tracking ref. Nothing in DevDesk moved it, so the column read `0` on a
repository forty commits behind.

`s` now does: sync fetches first and always, so a repository it touches — even
one it *refuses* to fast-forward — comes out with a true count. What remains is
that `loadEntries` still does not fetch, and must not: a directory listing that
hits the network on every drill-down is a different defect. So a repository not
synced since the app opened still shows a number nobody has checked. There is
now a way to make it true, and the one feature that acts on it never trusts it —
which is the difference between a lie and a stale reading.

**D34 — the explorer paginated nothing. Fixed.** Every list in
`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/api.go` was built with `PerPage: 100, Page: 1`, at
five sites, so a group with more than 100 subgroups or 100 projects was silently
truncated: the explorer showed fewer children than it had, and a recursive clone
skipped repositories without saying so.

`listAll` now walks every page and the four list calls go through it — one loop
rather than four copies, which is how one of them would have ended up wrong. It
terminates on `NextPage <= Page` rather than `NextPage == 0` alone: that also
stops a server pointing back at the page just served, and unlike a page cap it
is a bound that cannot cut a legitimate response short. `perPage` is the one
place the 100 is written.

Three tests assert both halves of a group's children and the pull's own walk
follow every page, and were checked against the pre-fix code — all three fail on
it. A fourth pins the runaway guard.

**D25 — status acted on the wrong monitor under a filter. Fixed** by §2 step 6,
which is also what found it. `getSelectedComponentIndex` replayed the sort by
hand and then indexed, but never applied the text filter the rows had already
been through; the SSL branch walked `m.components` by counting, unfiltered the
same way. Under a filter `e` edited and `ctrl+d` deleted a monitor the user was
not looking at. Same family as D24, and the ninth and last copy of the block.
`TestAFilteredSelectionEditsTheRowTheUserSees` was written before the fix and
failed on the old code.

**D24 — workspaces acted on the wrong directory under a filter. Fixed** by §2
step 5, which is also what found it. The rows were filtered and `m.entries` was
not, and every action resolved the cursor against `m.entries` — so under a
filter they acted on whatever sat at that index in the *unfiltered* list.
Filtering five entries down to `empty-dir` and pressing `ctrl+d` asked to delete
`devdesk`. `ctrl+s`, `r`, `enter`, `ctrl+o` and `ctrl+w` were all wrong the same
way. This is the defect class the component was built to remove, stated in its
package doc, and it was live in the one view where the consequence is a deleted
directory. `TestAFilteredSelectionActsOnTheRowTheUserSees` was written before
the fix and failed on the old code.

**D23 — an unreachable repository manager read as "not a group". Fixed** in
§3.8 step 3, which is also what found it. `NexusDetector.fetchRepoMeta` returned
one bare `ok=false` for both "the manager answered no" and "the manager could
not be asked", and `DetectGroup` collapsed both into `nil, nil`. Harmless while
the answer was discarded on every browser open; not harmless once step 3 cached
it, since one unreachable minute would have erased what was last known. The
error now propagates and a failed discovery is not written through.

**D21** also sat in that package but was **independent of §3.8**, and was fixed
without waiting for it — see §1.1.

D20 and D22 are fixed — see §1.1.

D15–D19 were found by the phase 5 pass, were unrelated to §3.8, and are fixed —
see §1.1. Each had been recorded with an inverted test asserting the broken
behaviour; those tests are what failed when the fix landed, and each has been
turned around to assert the fixed behaviour instead.

**D12 — `AuthEnabled` has no effect on browse or discovery. Fixed** (§3.8 step
2); the description below is what it was. The flag is
honoured in exactly three places: the `docker login` fired on form submit, the
`Logged` column, and the URL list `registryLoginStatusCmd` checks. Neither code
path that actually talks to a registry consults it. `submitSearch`
(`browser_keys.go:142`) calls `docker.GetStoredCreds(credURL)`
unconditionally and hands the result to `searchRegistryTagsCmd`;
`detectRegistryGroupCmd` (`commands.go:563`) does the same before calling into
`registrymgr`. A registry the user has marked as needing no authentication will
still have the host's stored credentials sent to it whenever any other registry
on that host has been logged into — which, given that Docker keys credentials by
host, is the normal case for a Nexus instance. This is the defect the
`anonymous` mode in §3.8 exists to make expressible; today there is no way to
say "do not send credentials here" at all.

**D13 — the browser cannot be dismissed while it is resolving.**
`handleKeyMsg` returns `nil` for every key in `browserStateResolving`
(`browser_keys.go:70`), `esc` included, and that state is entered
unconditionally on open whenever any registry is configured. The detections run
concurrently with an 8 s timeout each, so the wedge is bounded at roughly eight
seconds — but it is eight seconds during which the application ignores the user,
on a screen they may have opened by mistake. §3.8 removes the state rather than
the symptom: with members read from config and cache, there is nothing to
resolve and the form renders immediately.

A smaller thing in the same handler, not worth its own entry:
`HandleGroupDetected` matches the incoming result against `reg.URL`, so two
registries configured with the same URL collide and the second result overwrites
the first. The slug introduced in §3.8 is the natural key to match on instead.

**D14 — the registry filter shows a raw URL for group members.**
`registryFilterLabel()` (`browser_tags.go:63`) resolves the active filter by
searching `b.registries`, which holds only the configured top-level entries.
Discovered members are not in that list, so filtering to one falls through to
returning `b.registryFilter` — the full synthesised URL — where every other row
in the same view shows a short alias. The fix follows from §3.8 rather than
preceding it: once members are persisted they are resolvable, and the filter
gains a group level at the same time.

Pinned inverted by `TestAGroupMembersFilterLabelIsStillARawURL`, which asserts
the raw URL today and asserts the configured registry's alias alongside it as
the contrast.

**D21 is fixed** — see §1.1. It was the last entry in this section.

---

content.content:
### 3.21 The last four tables move to `datatable`

Sorti de §3.20 : le correctif du foreground n'atteint que les `datatable`, et
quatre tables n'en sont pas. Elles rendent leur texte dans la couleur par défaut
du terminal, sur laquelle le thème n'a pas prise, et elles ne peuvent pas être
corrigées là où elles sont — c'est la migration ou rien.

| Table | Fichier | Ce qu'elle fait à la main |
|---|---|---|
| Registries (onglet OCI) | `oci_resources/table.go:311`, `layout.go:56` | largeurs, curseur → objet par indice, **deux sources de lignes** |
| Tags du registry browser | `oci_resources/registry_browser.go:124` | largeurs, échange de styles au focus |
| Network inspect | `oci_resources/network_inspect_form.go:21` | largeurs, `SelectedContainer()` indexe `f.containers` |
| Résultats netdiag | `netdiag/view.go:152` | largeurs, **table reconstruite** à chaque mise à jour |

#### Pourquoi ça ne peut pas se régler sur place

`theme.DefaultTableStyles()` ne pose pas de foreground sur `Cell`, et lui en
poser un casserait la ligne sélectionnée de ces tables exactement comme il
casserait celle d'une `datatable` : les cellules sont rendues, puis la ligne
entière passe à `styles.Selected`, dont le reset intérieur referme le
surlignage au milieu. Le seul endroit où la couleur peut être décidée est un
renderer qui sait si la ligne est sélectionnée — et c'est ce que `datatable`
est.

#### Ce que chacune gagne d'autre

- **Rule 122 devient inexprimable.** Aujourd'hui elle n'y tient que par revue.
  Le danger est réel mais **latent** : `membersCell` rend
  `m.spinner.View() + "refreshing"` dans une cellule, et un spinner bubbles par
  défaut n'émet aucune séquence — vérifié, `View()` rend `"⣾ "` — donc rien ne
  bave aujourd'hui. Il suffit d'un `s.Style = …` pour que si.
- **Rule 116 en un seul endroit.** Les quatre recalculent leurs largeurs à la
  main ; `network_inspect_form` va jusqu'à écrire `columns[2].Width = available
  - flexName - fixedIPv4`, ce que le solveur fait pour toutes.
- **`Selected()` ne peut plus mentir.** Trois d'entre elles résolvent le curseur

### 3.18 A registry member is an address, not a URL — `repo_prefix`

Not started. §3.8 gave a group its members; this is about *reaching* one. It
closes D39. D40, which it needed closed with it, was fixed on its own — see
§1.1.

Found on 2026-08-10 trying to browse a single proxy inside a Nexus group. All
measurements below are from that instance — `pic-nexus.spw.dev.wallonie.be`, 64
repositories, 22 of them docker — and every one of them was an anonymous GET.

#### What was measured

Four ways to reach the same image, and no two of them derive from each other:

| Form | `…/tags/list` | What `docker pull` asks for | Pull |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** host, repo `dhi-io-proxy/eclipse-temurin` | 200 | `/v2/dhi-io-proxy/eclipse-temurin/…` → 200 | ✅ |
| **B** host `…/repository/dhi-io-proxy`, repo `eclipse-temurin` | 200 | `/v2/repository/dhi-io-proxy/…` → 404 | ❌ |
| **C** group subdomain, repo `eclipse-temurin` | 200 | `/v2/eclipse-temurin/…` → 200 | ✅ |
| **D** host, repo `docker-unsecure-group/eclipse-temurin` | 404 | — | — |

B is what `NexusDetector` builds today, and it is the one form that cannot pull.
D is the same trick as A applied to the group, and it does not work: a group is
reachable only through its own connector.

And A is settled **per repository**, not per instance:

| Proxy | A | B |
|---|---|---|
| `dhi-io-proxy` | 200 | 200 |
| `k8s-io-proxy` | 200 | 200 |
| `docker-io-proxy` | 404 | 200 |
| `quay-io-proxy` | 404 | 200 |

`docker-io-proxy/library/nginx` answering B and not A is the decisive pair: the
image is there and reachable, the path-prefix route is not. Whether a Docker
repository answers on a path prefix, a dedicated connector port or a subdomain is
a setting on **that repository** — `docker.httpPort`, `docker.httpsPort`,
`docker.subdomain`.

#### Why no synthesis can be right

Those three fields live in the repository's detailed configuration, behind
`GET /service/rest/v1/repositories/{format}/{type}/{name}` — which answers **403**
here for an ordinary pull account. The public
`GET /service/rest/v1/repositories/{name}` returns the summary shape,
`"attributes": {}`, carrying neither `memberNames` nor the connector fields.

So the one endpoint that would say what the members are is also the one that would
say how to reach them, and an instance that refuses it refuses both. That settles
the question the same way §3.8 decision F settled `provider`: **the addressing is
declared, not sniffed.** Guessing is what D39 already is.

#### The design — one field

`repo_prefix`, on `config.RegistryItem` and on `cache.RegistryGroupMember`. The
four connector modes collapse onto the pair `(url, repo_prefix)`:

| Mode | `url` | `repo_prefix` |
|---|---|---|
| path-based routing | `pic-nexus.spw.dev.wallonie.be` | `dhi-io-proxy` |
| HTTP/HTTPS connector | `pic-nexus.spw.dev.wallonie.be:8082` | — |
| subdomain routing | `dhi-io-proxy.spw.dev.wallonie.be` | — |
| group connector (form C) | `pic-nexus-docker-unsecure-group.spw…` | — |

Both directions derive from that one pair, which is the whole point: the prefix
goes in front of the repository name, the host stays `url`, and browse and pull
cannot disagree about which repository they mean — the disagreement being exactly
what D39 is.

Apply it **once**, in `submitSearch`, where the entry is in hand. The prefix is
then already part of `MultiRegistryTag.Repo`, so `multiImageName` needs no change
and neither does `registryAPIURL`. Teaching both of them about the prefix would
be two places free to drift — the same argument that gave the configuration view
one pointer accessor instead of a get/set pair.

#### What it unlocks

The request this came from: **one checkbox per proxy**. Declare a proxy per line
(`kind: registry`, `url: <host>`, `repo_prefix: dhi-io-proxy`) and the picker
built in §3.8 already does the rest. No discovery in the critical path — which
matters precisely because discovery is what is 403 here.

That is what **D40** had to be fixed for: those entries all share one host, and
until the picker keyed its selection on the entry rather than on the URL, one
per proxy meant one checkbox for all of them. It is fixed, so this no longer
waits on anything.

#### Scope

| Site | Change |
|---|---|
| `config.RegistryItem` | `repo_prefix` field; absent in an existing config and that stays valid |
| `config/registries.go` | validate at load: no leading or trailing `/`, refused on `kind: group` |
| `registrymgr.GroupMember` | carry a prefix instead of a synthesised URL |
| `NexusDetector` | emit `(host, prefix)`; leave the prefix empty when it cannot know |
| `cache.RegistryGroupMember` | carry it, so a discovered member can too |
| `RegistryForm` | one text field, shown for `kind: registry` |
| `submitSearch` | prepend the prefix to the repo, once |
| `entryFor` | resolve a result by entry key, not by URL — every member of a host answers to the same URL once the prefix carries the difference, so a result becomes unattributable (the one site D40 deliberately left alone) |
| `memberKey` | follow whatever tells two members apart once it is no longer the URL |
| Registries tab | show it — an entry whose URL is a bare host says nothing on its own |

Deliberately not done:

- **No probing to pick the form.** Trying A, then B, then a connector port is
  several requests per member per search to answer what the config can state, and
  it would make a member's address depend on which probe answered first.
- **No prefix on a group.** Form D is 404. A group's address is its connector,
  and that is its `url`.
- **No attempt to make `NexusDetector` fill the prefix in** where the detailed
  endpoint is refused. An empty prefix against a bare host is wrong and visibly
  so; a synthesised `/repository/` URL is wrong and plausible, which is D39.

#### Tests worth writing first

- A member with a prefix browses `<host>/v2/<prefix>/<repo>/tags/list` **and**
  pulls `<host>/<prefix>/<repo>:<tag>` — the pair D39 fails, so it fails on the
  current code.
- A member with no prefix produces byte-identical requests to today.
- A `repo_prefix` on a `kind: group` entry fails `LoadContext` rather than loading.

### 3.19 The dashboard stops reflowing, and gains resource charts — **done**

## 2. Technical debt

### Test coverage

**80.7 % overall — the agreed 80 % target is met.**

| Phase | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **done** except the `ui/theme` complement (~55 stmts) |
| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | **done** |
### Files over the 800-line ceiling

The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. **None now exceeds it.**

`internal/app/app.go` (1552 lines — the 1333 recorded earlier was stale) was the
last one. It was split into `keys.go`, `command_line.go`, `context.go`,
`theme.go`, `gitlab.go`, `scan_details.go`, `selection.go`, `help_overlay.go`
and `view.go`; the largest is 242 and `app.go` itself is 337. Unlike the earlier
splits this one was not purely mechanical, and the coverage figure moved with it
(72.4 % → 74.7 %): the two `maybe*` handlers, the two cached-result paths, the
two delegated-scan handlers and the two picker overlays were each one function
duplicated twice, and folding them together removed statements rather than
covering them. `New()` also gained a `newWithSize(cfg, w, h)` seam so the
constructor can be exercised — `New` itself reads the terminal size from
`os.Stdout` and panics when there is none, which is always the case under
`go test`.

`internal/ui/oci_resources/update.go` (1707 lines — the 1556 recorded earlier
was stale) was split into `keys.go`, `images.go`, `resources.go`,
`registries.go`, `results.go`, `launch.go`, `table.go`, `layout.go` and
`browser_bridge.go`; `update.go` itself is 364. `registry_browser.go` (918) was
split into `browser_keys.go`, `browser_tags.go`, `browser_state.go` and
`browser_view.go`; it is 243. The largest file in the package is now
`commands.go` at 598, which was already under the ceiling.

`internal/ui/security/model.go` (1991 lines, the largest file in the project)
was split into `update.go`, `form.go`, `scan.go`, `findings.go`, `details.go`,
`view.go`, `warnings.go`, `header.go` and `messages.go`; the largest is 299 and
`model.go` itself is 245. `warnings.go` is the one worth noticing: the
scan-error parser is pure string handling with no dependency on the model at
all, and pulling it out of a 2000-line file is what made it obvious it deserved
tests of its own.

`internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` (1114 lines) was split into `validation.go`,
### The race detector sees only what the tests run

**It runs locally now.** `mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C
compiler on `PATH`; without one it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`,
which is what this entry used to be about. The Windows development machine has
one — `gcc 16.1.0` (MinGW-w64, `x86_64-posix-seh`), with `go env CGO_ENABLED`
reading `1` and `CC` reading `gcc` — so the check is available before a push
rather than only after one.

Measured on 2026-08-14 with `go test -race -count=1 ./...`, so nothing came from
the test cache: **no data race, across all 29 packages that have tests** (three
have none). It costs two to three minutes wall-clock, and two packages are most
of it — `internal/ui/oci_resources` at 47 s and `internal/scan` at 33 s.

**CI still runs it, and that is not redundant.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs
`mise run test-race` on every push and pull request on `ubuntu-latest`. A race is
a scheduling accident, so a second machine with a different core count and a
different scheduler is a second sample rather than a repeat of the first — and
CI is what covers a contributor whose machine has no toolchain.

What has not changed is the limit worth keeping in mind: **the detector only
sees code the tests actually execute**, and coverage is 80.7 %. Rule 110
violations in untested paths remain invisible whichever machine runs it. The two
efforts compound, so this stays an argument for the coverage phases rather than a
substitute for them.

`internal/scan` is the package it has most to say about, since `Scanner.Scan` is
the only place in the application that fans out to concurrent goroutines writing
one shared result. Its tests drive all five stages at once, so that fan-out is
under the detector — and now under it locally, where a `Cmd` is being changed,
rather than only where the change is being reported on.

---

## 3. Planned features

What has not changed is the limit worth keeping in mind: **the detector only
sees code the tests actually execute**, and coverage is 80.7 %. Rule 110
violations in untested paths remain invisible whichever machine runs it. The two
efforts compound, so this stays an argument for the coverage phases rather than a
substitute for them.

`internal/scan` is the package it has most to say about, since `Scanner.Scan` is
the only place in the application that fans out to concurrent goroutines writing
one shared result. Its tests drive all five stages at once, so that fan-out is
under the detector — and now under it locally, where a `Cmd` is being changed,
rather than only where the change is being reported on.

---

1	// Package datatable is the shared mechanism behind the application's tables.
2	//
3	// What was shared before was only the *look* — theme.DefaultTableStyles,
4	// TableStylesForState/ForSeverity, components.FilterBar, theme.TimeAgo. Column
5	// widths, sorting, sort arrows, filter matching, cursor clamping and
6	// cursor-to-object resolution were written out again in each of the fifteen
7	// tables, and drifted:
8	//
9	//   - Rule 116's width invariant is broken by five of the twelve copies, which
10	//     clamp per column after the remainder has been computed (see widths.go).
11	//   - Two of eight clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks; the rest leave
12	//     it dangling, and oci_resources compensates by jumping to the top on every
13	//     filter toggle, throwing away the scroll position.
14	//   - Nine getSelectedX() replay filter-then-sort by hand to map a cursor back
15	//     to an object, with nothing tying that ordering to the one the rows were
16	//     built from. If they drift, the action lands on the wrong object and says
17	//     nothing. That is the duplication worth removing on correctness grounds.
18	//
19	// Here the filtered, sorted slice is built once and kept, so Selected() cannot
20	// disagree with what is on screen, and Cell func(T) string gives styled text
21	// nowhere to go — Rule 122 by construction rather than by review.
22	package datatable
23	
24	import (
25		"slices"
26		"sort"
27		"strings"
28	
29		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
30		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
31		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
32	
33		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
34		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
35	)
36	
37	// Column describes one column and how to get its value out of an item.
38	type Column[T any] struct {
39		Title string
40		// MinWidth is what the column asks for. It is a request, not a guarantee:
41		// when the terminal is too narrow for every request, the shortfall is
42		// shared out rather than each column defending its own floor.
43		MinWidth int
44		// Flex is the column's share of the space left over. 0 keeps it at
45		// MinWidth; the leftover is split between the flexible ones by weight.
46		Flex int
47		// Cell returns the text for this column. Plain text only: it is measured
48		// and truncated before anything is applied to it, and runewidth counts an
49		// escape sequence's bytes as width — a styled string is cut mid-escape and
50		// bleeds over every row below it (Rule 122). Taking a string rather than a
51		// styled value is what makes that unexpressible here.
52		Cell func(T) string
53		// Style colours the cell after it has been measured and truncated, which is
54		// the only order in which colour is safe (see render.go). Nil leaves the
55		// cell in the table's own colours.
56		//
57		// It is not consulted for the selected row: that row is handed to
58		// styles.Selected whole, and a colour inside it would end the highlight
59		// mid-row. A column cannot ask for that back.
60		Style func(T) lipgloss.Style
61		// Less sorts by this column. Nil means the column cannot be sorted by, and
62		// `.` skips it.
63		Less func(a, b T) bool
64		// Search is what the text filter matches against. Nil means the column does
65		// not participate.
66		Search func(T) string
67	}
68	
69	// Config is everything a view has to say about its table.
70	type Config[T any] struct {
71		Columns []Column[T]
72		// Tokens are the toggle filters shown in the bar (Rule 136).
73		Tokens []components.FilterToken
74		// TokenMatch decides whether an item passes the active toggles. Nil means
75		// the toggles are ignored, which is only sensible with no Tokens.
76		TokenMatch func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
77		// SortColumn is the column sorted by on open; -1 for no initial sort.
78		SortColumn int
79		// SortDesc opens the table on the descending order of SortColumn. It exists
80		// for the count columns, where ascending is the useless end: an inventory
81		// sorted by CRITICAL wants the worst target first, and cycling `.` past
82		// ascending to reach it on every open is not a default.
83		SortDesc bool
84		// SelectedStyles returns the table styles to use while the given item is
85		// under the cursor — that is the only thing bubbles/table can vary per
86		// selection, and it is what containers and security each re-derived by
87		// hand. Returning a style rather than a state keyword is what keeps this
88		// package from having to know what a severity is. Nil means the default.
89		SelectedStyles func(T) table.Styles
90	}
91	
92	// Model is a table over a slice of T.
93	type Model[T any] struct {
94		cfg   Config[T]
95		table table.Model
96		bar   components.FilterBar
97	
98		items []T
99		// visible is the filtered, sorted slice the rows were built from. Selected()
100		// reads it rather than recomputing, so the cursor cannot point at one
101		// ordering while the screen shows another.
102		visible []T
103	
104		// styles is what was last handed to the table. The rendering is this
105		// package's now (render.go) and bubbles keeps its copy unexported, so the
106		// styles have to be kept on this side to be readable at render time.
107		styles table.Styles
108		// offset is the first visible row — the scroll window bubbles kept in its
109		// viewport. clampOffset owns it.
110		offset int
111	
112		sortColumn int
113		sortDesc   bool
114		width      int
115	}
116	
117	// New builds a table from its configuration.
118	func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T] {
119		cols := make([]table.Column, len(cfg.Columns))
120		for i, c := range cfg.Columns {
121			cols[i] = table.Column{Title: c.Title, Width: c.MinWidth}
122		}
123		t := table.New(table.WithColumns(cols), table.WithFocused(true), table.WithHeight(10))
124	
125		bar := components.NewFilterBar()
126		if len(cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
127			bar = components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(cfg.Tokens)
128		}
129	
130		m := Model[T]{cfg: cfg, table: t, bar: bar, sortColumn: cfg.SortColumn, sortDesc: cfg.SortDesc}
131		// Through setStyles rather than the table alone: a table rendered before
132		// anything calls applyStyles — one built and drawn in the same frame — would
133		// otherwise render with the zero Styles, which carries no cell padding and
134		// so lays out two cells narrower per column than every width was solved for.
135		m.setStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
136		// The invariant the rest of the file rests on: sortColumn is either -1 or a
137		// column that can actually be sorted by. Settling it once here is what lets
138		// CycleSort and sorted() stop re-checking — and what stops `.` getting stuck
139		// flipping the direction of a column with no comparator.
140		if m.sortColumn >= len(cfg.Columns) || (m.sortColumn >= 0 && cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less == nil) {
141			m.sortColumn = -1
142			// A direction with no column to apply it to would put the header arrow
143			// on nothing and make `.` open on descending.
144			m.sortDesc = false
145		}
146		return m
147	}
148	
149	// SetItems replaces the contents. Filtering, sorting, row building and the
150	// cursor clamp all happen here and only here, which is what stops a cursor from
151	// being left pointing past the end — bubbles/table's SetRows does not clamp, and
152	// the stale cursor is invisible until the user presses a key.
153	func (m *Model[T]) SetItems(items []T) {
154		m.items = items
155		m.rebuild()
156	}
157	
158	// Items returns everything held, filtered or not.
159	func (m *Model[T]) Items() []T { return m.items }
160	
161	// Visible returns what is on screen, in the order it is on screen.
162	func (m *Model[T]) Visible() []T { return m.visible }
163	
164	// Selected returns the item under the cursor. The bool is false when there is
165	// nothing to select, which is the only case a caller has to handle.
166	func (m *Model[T]) Selected() (T, bool) {
167		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
168		if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(m.visible) {
169			var zero T
170			return zero, false
171		}
172		return m.visible[cursor], true
173	}
174	
175	// Cursor returns the selected row index.
176	func (m *Model[T]) Cursor() int { return m.table.Cursor() }
177	
178	// SetCursor puts the cursor on a row, clamped to what exists. Views that
179	// remember a position across a reload — workspaces restores one per directory
180	// level on the way back up — call this; nothing else should need it.
181	func (m *Model[T]) SetCursor(i int) {
182		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
183			return
184		}
185		m.table.SetCursor(min(max(i, 0), len(m.visible)-1))
186		m.afterCursorMove()
187	}
188	
189	// GotoTop moves the cursor to the first row. Views that want the cursor reset
190	// on a change of scope — security resets it when the tab changes — call this
191	// explicitly, because SetItems deliberately does not.
192	func (m *Model[T]) GotoTop() {
193		m.table.GotoTop()
194		m.afterCursorMove()
195	}
196	
197	// FilterBar exposes the bar for RenderFooter and GetFooterHeight (Rule 136).
198	func (m *Model[T]) FilterBar() *components.FilterBar { return &m.bar }
199	
200	// InEditMode reports whether the search field has the keyboard.
201	func (m *Model[T]) InEditMode() bool { return m.bar.InEditMode() }
202	
203	// Searchable reports whether anything can be filtered: a searchable column or a
204	// toggle token. Views use it to decide whether to advertise `/` (Rule 130).
205	func (m *Model[T]) Searchable() bool {
206		if len(m.cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
207			return true
208		}
209		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
210			if c.Search != nil {
211				return true
212			}
213		}
214		return false
215	}
216	
217	// Table exposes the underlying table for rendering.
218	func (m *Model[T]) Table() *table.Model { return &m.table }
219	
220	// SetHeight sets the number of rows shown. The window is re-clamped: a table
221	// that just got shorter can leave the cursor below its own last visible row.
222	func (m *Model[T]) SetHeight(h int) {
223		m.table.SetHeight(max(h, 1))
224		m.clampOffset()
225	}
226	
227	// Focus and Blur move the keyboard between two tables sharing a viewport, which
228	// is what the status view does with its monitors and its certificates.
229	func (m *Model[T]) Focus() {
230		m.table.Focus()
231		m.afterCursorMove()
232	}
233	
234	func (m *Model[T]) Blur() {
235		m.table.Blur()
236		m.setStyles(theme.BlurredTableStyles())
237	}
238	
239	// Resize recomputes the column widths for a viewport of this width (Rule 116).
240	// The width passed is the full viewport width, borders included; the borders and
241	// the per-cell padding are subtracted here so no caller has to remember to.
242	func (m *Model[T]) Resize(width, height int) {
243		m.width = width
244		widths := solveWidths(m.cfg.Columns, availableFor(width, len(m.cfg.Columns)))
245	
246		cols := m.table.Columns()
247		for i := range cols {
248			cols[i].Width = widths[i]
249			cols[i].Title = m.titleFor(i)
250		}
251		m.table.SetColumns(cols)
252		m.bar.Resize(width)
253		if height > 0 {
254			m.SetHeight(height)
255		}
256		m.afterCursorMove() // the selected row is pinned to this width
257	}
258	
259	// The sort arrows, and what they cost. Named because widths.go has to reserve
260	// room for them: a column's MinWidth is the view's statement about its content,
261	// and it knows nothing about two cells this package appends to the header.
262	const (
263		sortArrowAsc  = " ▲"
264		sortArrowDesc = " ▼"
265	)
266	
267	// titleFor returns a column's header, with a sort arrow on the active one.
268	func (m *Model[T]) titleFor(i int) string {
269		if i != m.sortColumn {
270			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title
271		}
272		if m.sortDesc {
273			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + sortArrowDesc
274		}
275		return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + sortArrowAsc
276	}
277	
278	// CycleSort advances the sort: ascending, descending, then on to the next
279	// sortable column (Rule 111's `.`). Returns to no sort after the last one when
280	// the table opened unsorted, so the original order stays reachable.
281	func (m *Model[T]) CycleSort() {
282		sortable := m.sortableColumns()
283		if len(sortable) == 0 {
284			return
285		}
286		switch {
287		case m.sortColumn < 0:
288			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = sortable[0], false
289		case !m.sortDesc:
290			m.sortDesc = true
291		default:
292			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = m.nextSortable(sortable), false
293		}
294		m.rebuild()
295		m.Resize(m.width, 0) // the arrow moved
296	}
297	
298	// nextSortable returns the column after the current one, wrapping to the first —
299	// or to -1 when the table opened unsorted, so "no sort" is a stop on the cycle.
300	//
301	// slices.Index rather than a loop with a trailing fallback: the current column
302	// is always in sortable (New guarantees it), and a fallback that cannot run is
303	// a branch nothing can ever check.
304	func (m *Model[T]) nextSortable(sortable []int) int {
305		if at := slices.Index(sortable, m.sortColumn); at+1 < len(sortable) {
306			return sortable[at+1]
307		}
308		if m.cfg.SortColumn < 0 {
309			return -1
310		}
311		return sortable[0]
312	}
313	
314	func (m *Model[T]) sortableColumns() []int {
315		var out []int
316		for i, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
317			if c.Less != nil {
318				out = append(out, i)
319			}
320		}
321		return out
322	}
323	
324	// SortState reports the column sorted by and its direction, for tests and for
325	// views that show it elsewhere. Column is -1 when nothing is sorted.
326	func (m *Model[T]) SortState() (column int, desc bool) { return m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc }
327	
328	// Update handles the keys every table shares: navigation, `/` for the search,
329	// `.` for the sort, and whatever the filter bar takes while it is focused.
330	// Anything else is left alone, so the view keeps its own actions.
331	func (m *Model[T]) Update(msg tea.Msg) tea.Cmd {
332		if m.bar.InEditMode() {
333			var cmd tea.Cmd
334			m.bar, cmd = m.bar.Update(msg)
335			m.rebuild()
336			return cmd
337		}
338	
339		key, ok := msg.(tea.KeyMsg)
340		if !ok {
341			return nil
342		}
343		switch key.String() {
344		case "/":
345			// A table with nothing to search does not claim the key: activating a
346			// search that can only ever match nothing would empty the list, and the
347			// bar the user needs to see why is not in that view's footer.
348			if !m.Searchable() {
349				return nil
350			}
351			return m.bar.ActivateSearch()
352		case ".":
353			m.CycleSort()
354		case "up", "k":
355			m.table.MoveUp(1)
356			m.afterCursorMove()
357		case "down", "j":
358			m.table.MoveDown(1)
359			m.afterCursorMove()
360		case "pgup":
361			m.table.MoveUp(m.table.Height())
362			m.afterCursorMove()
363		case "pgdown":
364			m.table.MoveDown(m.table.Height())
365			m.afterCursorMove()
366		case "g", "home":
367			m.table.GotoTop()
368			m.afterCursorMove()
369		case "G", "end":
370			m.table.GotoBottom()
371			m.afterCursorMove()
372		}
373		return nil
374	}
375	
376	// SetTokenActive toggles one of the bar's filter tokens and re-applies it.
377	func (m *Model[T]) SetTokenActive(label string, active bool) {
378		m.bar.SetTokenActive(label, active)
379		m.rebuild()
380	}
381	
382	// IsTokenActive reports whether a toggle filter is on.
383	func (m *Model[T]) IsTokenActive(label string) bool { return m.bar.IsTokenActive(label) }
384	
385	// rebuild filters, sorts, writes the rows and puts the cursor somewhere real.
386	func (m *Model[T]) rebuild() {
387		m.visible = m.sorted(m.filtered())
388	
389		rows := make([]table.Row, len(m.visible))
390		for i, item := range m.visible {
391			cells := make(table.Row, len(m.cfg.Columns))
392			for j, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
393				cells[j] = c.Cell(item)
394			}
395			rows[i] = cells
396		}
397		m.table.SetRows(rows)
398	
399		// bubbles/table leaves the cursor where it was, so a list that just got
400		// shorter strands it past the end until the user presses a key. It also
401		// reports -1 while there are no rows at all, and that has to be taken back
402		// when rows return — a filter typed past its last match and then corrected
403		// would otherwise leave the table showing rows none of which is selected.
404		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
405		case len(rows) == 0:
406			// -1 is bubbles' own "nothing selected", and what it reports for a
407			// table that never had rows. Leaving the old index would make an empty
408			// list the one state where the cursor points past the end.
409			m.table.SetCursor(-1)
410		case cursor >= len(rows):
411			m.table.SetCursor(len(rows) - 1)
412		case cursor < 0:
413			m.table.SetCursor(0)
414		}
415		m.afterCursorMove()
416	}
417	
418	// afterCursorMove is what every cursor, height and item change ends with: the
419	// styles follow the selected item, and the scroll window follows the cursor.
420	// Keeping them on one call is what stops a new call site from remembering one
421	// and forgetting the other — the offset was invisible while bubbles owned it.
422	func (m *Model[T]) afterCursorMove() {
423		m.clampOffset()
424		m.applyStyles()
425	}
426	
427	// applyStyles asks the view for the styles that go with the selected item.
428	func (m *Model[T]) applyStyles() {
429		if !m.table.Focused() {
430			return // Blur owns the styles until Focus takes them back
431		}
432		styles := theme.DefaultTableStyles()
433		if item, ok := m.Selected(); ok && m.cfg.SelectedStyles != nil {
434			styles = m.cfg.SelectedStyles(item)
435		}
436		// Pin the selected row to the full content width. Column widths are counted
437		// in cells, and a Nerd Font icon does not always render as wide as it
438		// counts, so the highlight otherwise stops short of the right border by
439		// however much the row's icons disagreed. Padding to a width the row can
440		// never exceed is a no-op when they agree.
441		if m.width > 2 {
442			styles.Selected = styles.Selected.Width(m.width - 2)
443		}
444		m.setStyles(styles)
445	}
446	
447	// setStyles keeps bubbles' copy and this package's in step. The rendering reads
448	// the one here (render.go); bubbles' is still what Table() reports, which the
449	// tests and any view reaching for the raw table expect to be current.
450	func (m *Model[T]) setStyles(styles table.Styles) {
451		m.styles = styles
452		m.table.SetStyles(styles)
453	}
454	
455	// filtered applies the search query and the toggle filters.
456	func (m *Model[T]) filtered() []T {
457		query := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(m.bar.SearchQuery()))
458		active := m.activeTokens()
459	
460		out := make([]T, 0, len(m.items))
461		for _, item := range m.items {
462			if m.cfg.TokenMatch != nil && !m.cfg.TokenMatch(item, active) {
463				continue
464			}
465			if query != "" && !m.matchesQuery(item, query) {
466				continue
467			}
468			out = append(out, item)
469		}
470		return out
471	}
472	
473	func (m *Model[T]) activeTokens() map[string]bool {
474		active := make(map[string]bool, len(m.cfg.Tokens))
475		for _, tok := range m.cfg.Tokens {
476			if m.bar.IsTokenActive(tok.Label) {
477				active[tok.Label] = true
478			}
479		}
480		return active
481	}
482	
483	// matchesQuery tests the query against each searchable column and then against
484	// the row as a whole.
485	//
486	// The row-level pass is what keeps a query spanning two fields — "tcp 22" over a
487	// ports list — working: netdiag matched against a joined haystack while the
488	// other four filter loops matched per field, and per field alone would have
489	// quietly dropped those matches on migration. Matching both ways is a superset
490	// of either, so no view loses anything and they all gain the same thing.
491	func (m *Model[T]) matchesQuery(item T, query string) bool {
492		var joined strings.Builder
493		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
494			if c.Search == nil {
495				continue
496			}
497			value := c.Search(item)
498			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value), query) {
499				return true
500			}
501			if joined.Len() > 0 {
502				joined.WriteByte(' ')
503			}
504			joined.WriteString(value)
505		}
506		return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(joined.String()), query)
507	}
508	
509	// sorted orders the visible slice. SliceStable, because sort.Slice is not and
510	// two rows equal on the sort column would otherwise swap between rebuilds.
511	func (m *Model[T]) sorted(items []T) []T {
512		if m.sortColumn < 0 {
513			return items
514		}
515		less := m.cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less // never nil — see New
516		desc := m.sortDesc
517		sort.SliceStable(items, func(i, j int) bool {
518			if desc {
519				return less(items[j], items[i])
520			}
521			return less(items[i], items[j])
522		})
523		return items
524	}
525

ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)

1	package ociresources
2	
3	import (
4		"strings"
5	
6		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
7		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/docker"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
11	)
12	
13	// viewportOverhead is the number of lines consumed by the top padding and table borders in the viewport.
14	const viewportOverhead = 3 // EmptyLine + table header + table border
15	
16	// NetworkInspectForm displays the containers connected to a Docker network in the viewport.
17	type NetworkInspectForm struct {
18		networkID   string
19		networkName string
20		containers  []docker.NetworkContainer
21		table       table.Model
22		loading     bool
23		width       int
24		height      int
25	}
26	
27	// newNetworkInspectForm creates a NetworkInspectForm for the given network.
28	func newNetworkInspectForm(networkID, networkName string, width, height int) *NetworkInspectForm {
29		columns := []table.Column{
30			{Title: "Container", Width: 30},
31			{Title: "IPv4", Width: 18},
32			{Title: "MAC Address", Width: 18},
33		}
34		t := table.New(
35			table.WithColumns(columns),
36			table.WithFocused(true),
37			table.WithHeight(10),
38		)
39		t.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
40	
41		f := &NetworkInspectForm{
42			networkID:   networkID,
43			networkName: networkName,
44			loading:     true,
45			width:       width,
46			height:      height,
47			table:       t,
48		}
49		f.resize(width, height)
50		return f
51	}
52	
53	// SetContainers updates the table with the fetched containers.
54	func (f *NetworkInspectForm) SetContainers(containers []docker.NetworkContainer) {
55		f.loading = false
56		f.containers = containers
57		rows := make([]table.Row, len(containers))
58		for i, c := range containers {
59			rows[i] = table.Row{c.Name, c.IPv4, c.MacAddress}
60		}
61		f.table.SetRows(rows)
62	}
63	
64	// SelectedContainer returns the currently selected container or nil.
65	func (f *NetworkInspectForm) SelectedContainer() *docker.NetworkContainer {
66		cursor := f.table.Cursor()
67		if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(f.containers) {
68			return nil
69		}
70		c := f.containers[cursor]
71		return &c
72	}
73	
74	// Update handles input for the network inspect form.
75	func (f *NetworkInspectForm) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*NetworkInspectForm, tea.Cmd) {
76		switch msg := msg.(type) {
77		case tea.KeyMsg:
78			switch msg.String() {
79			case "up", "k":
80				f.table.MoveUp(1)
81			case "down", "j":
82				f.table.MoveDown(1)
83			case "g", "home":
84				f.table.GotoTop()
85			case "G", "end":
86				f.table.GotoBottom()
87			}
88		}
89		return f, nil
90	}
91	
92	// resize adjusts the table columns and height to fit the viewport.
93	func (f *NetworkInspectForm) resize(width, height int) {
94		f.width = width
95		f.height = height
96	
97		// Rule 116: available = width - 2 (viewport borders) - numCols × 2 (cell padding)
98		numCols := 3
99		available := width - 2 - numCols*2
100		fixedIPv4 := 16
101		fixedMAC := 20
102		flexName := max(available-fixedIPv4-fixedMAC, 10)
103		columns := f.table.Columns()
104		if len(columns) >= 3 {
105			columns[0].Width = flexName
106			columns[1].Width = fixedIPv4
107			columns[2].Width = available - flexName - fixedIPv4
108			f.table.SetColumns(columns)
109		}
110	
111		tableH := max(height-viewportOverhead, 3)
112		f.table.SetHeight(tableH)
113	}
114	
115	// View renders the network inspect form in the viewport (Rule 112).
116	func (f *NetworkInspectForm) View() string {
117		w := f.width
118		lines := []string{theme.EmptyLineBg(w)} // Rule 131: top padding
119	
120		if f.loading {
121			lines = append(lines,
122				theme.PadWithBg(theme.DimStyle.Render("  Loading containers..."), w),
123			)
124		} else if len(f.containers) == 0 {
125			lines = append(lines,
126				theme.PadWithBg(theme.DimStyle.Render("  No containers connected to this network."), w),
127			)
128		} else {
129			lines = append(lines, f.table.View())
130		}
131	
132		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
133	}

1	package datatable
2	
3	import (
4		"strings"
5	
6		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
7		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
8		"github.com/mattn/go-runewidth"
9	
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
11	)
12	
13	// Why this package renders its own rows rather than calling table.Model.View().
14	//
15	// bubbles/table builds a cell as:
16	//
17	//	m.styles.Cell.Render(style.Render(runewidth.Truncate(value, width, "…")))
18	//
19	// — it measures the value *before* styling it, with runewidth, which counts an
20	// escape sequence's bytes as width. A seven-cell string carrying a colour
21	// measures 28, so it is truncated in a column twice wide enough, and the cut
22	// lands inside the escape: "\x1b[38;2;166;2…". The unterminated sequence then
23	// bleeds over every row below. That is Rule 122, and no configuration of
24	// bubbles avoids it — bubbles v1.0.0 has the same line.
25	//
26	// Here the order is inverted: Cell returns plain text, which is what gets
27	// measured and truncated, and Style is applied to the finished cell. Nothing
28	// styled is ever measured, so the failure is unexpressible rather than
29	// forbidden by review.
30	//
31	// The other half of the reason is the selected row. bubbles hands the whole
32	// joined row to styles.Selected, and a colour inside it closes with a reset
33	// that takes the selection background with it for the rest of the line — the
34	// highlight ends mid-row. So per-cell colours are dropped on the selected row
35	// (see cellStyle), which is the one place the row keeps rendering exactly as it
36	// did before.
37	
38	// truncationMarker ends a cell too narrow for its content.
39	const truncationMarker = "…"
40	
41	// View renders the header and the window of rows around the cursor.
42	func (m *Model[T]) View() string {
43		cols := m.table.Columns()
44		// At least one line under the header. A terminal too short to hold a single
45		// row leaves Height() at 0, and a table that renders literally nothing
46		// closes the viewport border onto itself — bubbles' viewport always emitted
47		// that line, and two views check for it at 20x1.
48		rows := max(m.table.Height(), 1)
49	
50		lines := make([]string, 0, rows+1)
51		lines = append(lines, m.headerLine(cols))
52	
53		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
54		for i := m.offset; i < len(m.visible) && len(lines) <= rows; i++ {
55			lines = append(lines, m.rowLine(cols, m.visible[i], i == cursor))
56		}
57		// Pad to the full height so the viewport border does not close in on a
58		// short list. bubbles' viewport did this with unstyled lines; filling them
59		// with the app background is Rule 115 applied to the one part of the table
60		// that had escaped it.
61		blank := theme.EmptyLineBg(contentWidth(cols))
62		for len(lines) <= rows {
63			lines = append(lines, blank)
64		}
65		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
66	}
67	
68	// contentWidth is what the rendered lines span: every column plus the padding
69	// bubbles adds around each. It equals the viewport width less its two borders
70	// whenever Rule 116 holds, but it is measured rather than assumed so that a
71	// table that has never been resized still pads to its own content.
72	func contentWidth(cols []table.Column) int {
73		width := 0
74		for _, col := range cols {
75			if col.Width > 0 {
76				width += col.Width + cellPadding
77			}
78		}
79		return width
80	}
81	
82	// headerLine renders the column titles, sort arrow included.
83	func (m *Model[T]) headerLine(cols []table.Column) string {
84		var line strings.Builder
85		for _, col := range cols {
86			if col.Width <= 0 {
87				continue
88			}
89			line.WriteString(m.styles.Header.Render(fit(col.Title, col.Width)))
90		}
91		return line.String()
92	}
93	
94	// rowLine renders one row.
95	func (m *Model[T]) rowLine(cols []table.Column, item T, selected bool) string {
96		var line strings.Builder
97		for i, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
98			if i >= len(cols) || cols[i].Width <= 0 {
99				continue
100			}
101			line.WriteString(m.cellStyle(c, item, selected).Render(fit(c.Cell(item), cols[i].Width)))
102		}
103		if selected {
104			return m.styles.Selected.Render(line.String())
105		}
106		return line.String()
107	}
108	
109	// fit truncates the text to the column and pads it out, emitting no escape
110	// sequence of its own — the caller styles what comes back. Doing it in that
111	// order is the whole point of this file: runewidth counts an escape sequence's
112	// bytes as width, so text has to be measured while it is still plain.
113	func fit(text string, width int) string {
114		return lipgloss.NewStyle().Width(width).MaxWidth(width).Inline(true).
115			Render(runewidth.Truncate(text, width, truncationMarker))
116	}
117	
118	// cellStyle is the style one cell is rendered with.
119	//
120	// On the selected row the column's own colours are dropped and the row is
121	// handed to styles.Selected whole, exactly as bubbles did: a colour inside it
122	// closes with a reset that takes the selection background with it for the rest
123	// of the line. The highlight answers "where am I", and no per-cell colour is
124	// worth losing it to.
125	//
126	// Off the selected row every cell carries an explicit foreground **and**
127	// background, whether or not the column asked for either. Both halves are
128	// forced for the same reason and each fixes its own defect:
129	//
130	//   - Background: lipgloss does not inherit one (Rule 115), and the app's
131	//     viewport style only reaches the cells that emit nothing of their own. One
132	//     coloured cell would otherwise end its line with a reset and strip the
133	//     background from everything to its right.
134	//   - Foreground: neither theme.DefaultTableStyles() nor bubbles' own sets one
135	//     on Cell, so a column that declares no Style rendered in whatever
136	//     foreground the terminal happens to use — the theme had no say. Four views
137	//     had written `Foreground(theme.ColorText)` into a Style of their own to get
138	//     it back, which is the shape a missing default takes.
139	//
140	// **Il ne peut pas être mis sur `styles.Cell`, et c'est ce qui décide où il
141	// va.** Les cellules sont rendues puis la ligne entière est passée à
142	// `styles.Selected` : une couleur de cellule y ouvre une séquence dont le reset
143	// referme le surlignage au milieu de la ligne. C'est le défaut de la Rule 122,
144	// et la seule parade est de décider la couleur par cellule, ici, où l'on sait si
145	// la ligne est sélectionnée.
146	func (m *Model[T]) cellStyle(c Column[T], item T, selected bool) lipgloss.Style {
147		if selected {
148			// Ni fond ni texte ici : ils masqueraient ceux de styles.Selected.
149			return m.styles.Cell
150		}
151		if c.Style == nil {
152			return m.styles.Cell.Foreground(theme.ColorText).Background(theme.ColorBackground)
153		}
154		style := c.Style(item).Padding(0, 1)
155		if _, unset := style.GetForeground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
156			style = style.Foreground(theme.ColorText)
157		}
158		if _, unset := style.GetBackground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
159			style = style.Background(theme.ColorBackground)
160		}
161		return style
162	}
163	
164	// clampOffset moves the scroll window the least it can to keep the cursor in
165	// it. bubbles kept this in an unexported viewport; owning the rendering means
166	// owning the offset too.
167	//
168	// The window is only moved when the cursor has left it, so a reload that keeps
169	// the cursor on screen keeps the scroll position — the property SetItems was
170	// written to protect.
171	func (m *Model[T]) clampOffset() {
172		height := max(m.table.Height(), 1)
173		last := max(len(m.visible)-height, 0)
174	
175		m.offset = min(max(m.offset, 0), last)
176	
177		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
178		case cursor < 0: // nothing selected: an empty table scrolls nowhere
179			m.offset = 0
180		case cursor < m.offset:
181			m.offset = cursor
182		case cursor >= m.offset+height:
183			m.offset = cursor - height + 1
184		}
185	}
186	
187	// Offset reports the first visible row, for tests that check the window
188	// follows the cursor without going through the rendered string.
189	func (m *Model[T]) Offset() int { return m.offset }
190

1	package explorer
2	
3	import (
4		"strings"
5	
6		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
7		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/datatable"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
11	)
12	
13	// cloneState is what one row of the clone list is doing.
14	//
15	// There are five, and only five, because decision 2 draws the line: the
16	// explorer creates what is missing and never reconciles what exists. A dirty
17	// working copy, a diverged branch, a stale remote — none of them is a state
18	// here, they belong to the workspaces view (§3.17).
19	type cloneState int
20	
21	const (
22		cloneQueued cloneState = iota
23		cloneRunning
24		cloneCloned
25		cloneAlreadyThere
26		cloneFailed
27	)
28	
29	// cloneRow is one repository, or one group whose walk failed.
30	type cloneRow struct {
31		path  string
32		state cloneState
33		// frame is the spinner's current character, stamped on while the row is
34		// running. It is text rather than a rendered spinner because a table cell
35		// must carry no escape sequences (Rule 122).
36		frame  string
37		detail string
38	}
39	
40	// cloneList is the ModeCloning screen: the pipeline in flight and the table
41	// showing it. It is the progress view and the report both — decision 9 leaves
42	// modals for yes/no confirmations only.
43	type cloneList struct {
44		table datatable.Model[cloneRow]
45		// rows is the authoritative order: discovery order, which is the order
46		// things happened. The table may sort it, but the list does not.
47		rows  []cloneRow
48		index map[string]int
49	
50		run    *cloneRun
51		target string
52		// frameIdx indexes spinner.Dot.Frames directly rather than reading the
53		// view's spinner: spinner.Model.View() renders through its style, and a
54		// styled string in a table cell bleeds over every row below it (Rule 122).
55		frameIdx int
56	
57		// cancelling is set by `esc` and cleared by nothing: a run that is stopping
58		// cannot be restarted, only awaited. A second `esc` must not force, because
59		// forcing is the half-cloned directory decision 12 avoids.
60		cancelling bool
61		finished   bool
62	}
63	
64	const (
65		colCloneStatusMin = 16
66		colClonePathMin   = 30
67		colCloneDetailMin = 20
68	)
69	
70	func newCloneList(target string, run *cloneRun) *cloneList {
71		return &cloneList{
72			target: target,
73			run:    run,
74			index:  map[string]int{},
75			table: datatable.New(datatable.Config[cloneRow]{
76				Columns: cloneColumns(),
77				// Discovery order, deliberately: it is the order things happened, and
78				// a list that reorders itself while it fills is unreadable. `.` still
79				// sorts on demand.
80				SortColumn: -1,
81			}),
82		}
83	}
84	
85	// cloneColumns describes the clone list.
86	func cloneColumns() []datatable.Column[cloneRow] {
87		return []datatable.Column[cloneRow]{
88			{
89				Title: "Status", MinWidth: colCloneStatusMin,
90				Cell:  func(r cloneRow) string { return cloneStatusLabel(r) },
91				Style: cloneStatusStyle,
92				Less:  func(a, b cloneRow) bool { return a.state < b.state },
93			},
94			{
95				Title: "Repository", MinWidth: colClonePathMin, Flex: 2,
96				Cell:   func(r cloneRow) string { return r.path },
97				Less:   func(a, b cloneRow) bool { return strings.ToLower(a.path) < strings.ToLower(b.path) },
98				Search: func(r cloneRow) string { return r.path },
99			},
100			{
101				Title: "Detail", MinWidth: colCloneDetailMin, Flex: 1,
102				Cell:   func(r cloneRow) string { return r.detail },
103				Search: func(r cloneRow) string { return r.detail },
104			},
105		}
106	}
107	
108	// cloneStatusLabel is the status cell: an icon and a word, plain text.
109	func cloneStatusLabel(r cloneRow) string {
110		switch r.state {
111		case cloneRunning:
112			return r.frame + " cloning"
113		case cloneCloned:
114			return theme.IconOK + " cloned"
115		case cloneAlreadyThere:
116			return theme.IconSkipped + " already there"
117		case cloneFailed:
118			return theme.IconError + " failed"
119		default:
120			return theme.IconPending + " queued"
121		}
122	}
123	
124	// cloneStatusStyle colours the status cell.
125	//
126	// The five states are the whole vocabulary of this screen, and they are the one
127	// thing a run of forty rows is read for: which ones failed, which are still
128	// going, which were already on disk and were left alone.
129	func cloneStatusStyle(r cloneRow) lipgloss.Style {
130		switch r.state {
131		case cloneCloned:
132			return theme.StatusOKStyle
133		case cloneFailed:
134			return theme.StatusErrorStyle
135		case cloneRunning:
136			return lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight)
137		default: // queued, and already there — neither is news
138			return theme.DimStyle
139		}
140	}
141	
142	// apply folds one pipeline event into the list.
143	//
144	// An event for a path that has no row yet creates one. That is not defensive
145	// padding: cloneWalkFailed names a group, which was never found as a
146	// repository and so has no row to update.
147	func (l *cloneList) apply(event cloneEvent) {
148		switch event.kind {
149		case cloneFound:
150			l.upsert(event.path, cloneQueued, "")
151		case cloneBegan:
152			l.upsert(event.path, cloneRunning, "")
153		case cloneEnded:
154			switch {
155			case event.err != nil:
156				l.upsert(event.path, cloneFailed, event.err.Error())
157			case event.skipped:
158				l.upsert(event.path, cloneAlreadyThere, "")
159			default:
160				l.upsert(event.path, cloneCloned, "")
161			}
162		case cloneWalkFailed:
163			l.upsert(event.path, cloneFailed, "discovery: "+event.err.Error())
164		}
165		l.sync()
166	}
167	
168	func (l *cloneList) upsert(path string, state cloneState, detail string) {
169		if i, ok := l.index[path]; ok {
170			l.rows[i].state = state
171			l.rows[i].detail = detail
172			return
173		}
174		l.index[path] = len(l.rows)
175		l.rows = append(l.rows, cloneRow{path: path, state: state, detail: detail})
176	}
177	
178	// advance moves the spinner shown on the running rows one frame on.
179	func (l *cloneList) advance() {
180		l.frameIdx = (l.frameIdx + 1) % len(spinner.Dot.Frames)
181		l.sync()
182	}
183	
184	// sync hands the table a copy with the current spinner frame stamped on.
185	//
186	// The frame is stamped here rather than held on the row because it belongs to
187	// the list, not to any repository: one spinner, on every row that is running.
188	func (l *cloneList) sync() {
189		frame := spinner.Dot.Frames[l.frameIdx%len(spinner.Dot.Frames)]
190		items := make([]cloneRow, len(l.rows))
191		copy(items, l.rows)
192		for i := range items {
193			if items[i].state == cloneRunning {
194				items[i].frame = frame
195			}
196		}
197		l.table.SetItems(items)
198	}
199	
200	// running counts the clones still in flight, which is what `esc` has to wait
201	// for and what the view states while it does.
202	func (l *cloneList) running() int {
203		n := 0
204		for _, r := range l.rows {
205			if r.state == cloneRunning {
206				n++
207			}
208		}
209		return n
210	}
211	
212	// counts is the header line: what has been found and how it went.
213	func (l *cloneList) counts() (found, cloned, present, failed int) {
214		for _, r := range l.rows {
215			found++
216			switch r.state {
217			case cloneCloned:
218				cloned++
219			case cloneAlreadyThere:
220				present++
221			case cloneFailed:
222				failed++
223			case cloneQueued, cloneRunning:
224			}
225		}
226		return found, cloned, present, failed
227	}
228	
229	// failures returns the failed paths, for the log and the footer. Decision 13
230	// discards the list on `esc`, and workspaces records only the successes — a
231	// failure that wrote nothing leaves nothing behind, so it has to be said while
232	// the view is still alive.
233	func (l *cloneList) failures() []string {
234		var out []string
235		for _, r := range l.rows {
236			if r.state == cloneFailed {
237				out = append(out, r.path)
238			}
239		}
240		return out
241	}

1	package ociresources
2	
3	import (
4		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
5		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
6		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
7	
8		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/cache"
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
11	)
12	
13	// browserState tracks which screen the browser is on.
14	type browserState int
15	
16	// browserStateResolving is gone. The browser used to open into it and ignore
17	// every key — esc included — while up to one 8-second detection per configured
18	// registry ran (D13). Members now come from config plus the group cache, so
19	// there is nothing to resolve and the form renders at once, offline included.
20	const (
21		browserStateInput  browserState = iota // search form
22		browserStateTags                       // results table
23		browserStateStatus                     // spinner during pull
24	)
25	
26	// browserRegistryEntry is one selectable registry in the browser form.
27	// Group members have ParentSlug set; standalone registries have it empty.
28	type browserRegistryEntry struct {
29		URL   string
30		Alias string
31		// Slug identifies the entry: its own for a standalone registry, its group's
32		// for a member. It is what the result filter resolves labels through, and
33		// what replaced matching on URL — two registries configured with the same
34		// URL used to collide.
35		Slug        string
36		ParentAlias string // non-empty = member of a group
37		ParentSlug  string
38		parentURL   string // URL of the parent RegistryItem (for credential lookup)
39		// key identifies the entry among all the others, and is what the checkbox
40		// and the remembered exclusions are keyed on (D40). It is not the URL: two
41		// registries may be declared on one host — the form enforces slug
42		// uniqueness, not URL uniqueness — and §3.18 makes that the ordinary case.
43		// Nor is it Slug, which holds the *group's* slug for a member and would
44		// give a whole group one checkbox. So: the slug for a standalone registry,
45		// and the group's slug plus the member's URL for a member, the URL being
46		// what tells two members of one group apart. Their aliases do not:
47		// cleanMemberAlias strips `-proxy` and `-hosted`, so `docker-io-proxy` and
48		// `docker-io-hosted` both display as `docker-io`.
49		key string
50		// authMode is already resolved: a member carries what its group settled on,
51		// since `inherit` is the only thing the shared credential entry can mean.
52		authMode string
53	}
54	
55	// resultFilter narrows the tag table to one group or one registry. Both empty
56	// means everything.
57	type resultFilter struct {
58		groupSlug string
59		url       string
60	}
61	
62	func (f resultFilter) isEmpty() bool { return f.groupSlug == "" && f.url == "" }
63	
64	// matches reports whether a result from url passes the filter. A group matches
65	// every member's URL, which is what the group level is for.
66	func (f resultFilter) matches(url string, entry *browserRegistryEntry) bool {
67		switch {
68		case f.isEmpty():
69			return true
70		case f.groupSlug != "":
71			return entry != nil && entry.ParentSlug == f.groupSlug
72		default:
73			return url == f.url
74		}
75	}
76	
77	// pickerRow is one line of the registry picker. A group is a row of its own
78	// whose checkbox covers its members, which is the only way to select eight
79	// proxies without eight keystrokes.
80	type pickerRow struct {
81		// groupSlug is set on a group header; entry is -1 there.
82		groupSlug string
83		label     string
84		entry     int // index into b.entries, or -1
85	}
86	
87	const brFieldRepo = 0
88	
89	// brFieldReg returns the form field index for the i-th picker row.
90	func (b *RegistryBrowser) brFieldReg(i int) int { return 1 + i }
91	
92	// brFieldSubmit returns the form field index for the Browse Tags button.
93	func (b *RegistryBrowser) brFieldSubmit() int { return 1 + len(b.rows) }
94	
95	// RegistryBrowserCloseMsg is sent when the user presses ESC on the browser input screen.
96	type RegistryBrowserCloseMsg struct{}
97	
98	// tagSortField selects which column to sort the tag list by.
99	type tagSortField int
100	
101	const (
102		tagSortByName    tagSortField = iota
103		tagSortByUpdated              // newest first
104	)
105	
106	// RegistryBrowser searches image tags across multiple configured registries.
107	type RegistryBrowser struct {
108		registries    []config.RegistryItem
109		width, height int
110	
111		// Entries, built once from config plus the group cache.
112		entries []browserRegistryEntry
113		rows    []pickerRow
114	
115		// Form state
116		repoInput    textinput.Model
117		selectedRegs map[string]bool // entry key → checked
118		focusedField int
119	
120		// Results state
121		tags              []MultiRegistryTag
122		pendingSearches   int
123		registryFilter    resultFilter
124		tagTable          table.Model
125		scanCache         map[string]cache.ImageScanEntry
126		scanningTags      map[string]bool
127		tagScanSpinnerIdx int
128	
129		// Tag filter/sort in results view
130		filterInput  textinput.Model
131		filterActive bool
132		tagSortCol   tagSortField
133		tagSortDesc  bool
134	
135		// Status screen (pull operation)
136		spinner   spinner.Model
137		operation string
138		imageName string
139	
140		state browserState
141	}
142	
143	// newRegistryBrowser creates a RegistryBrowser showing its form immediately.
144	//
145	// A group's members come from the cache the Registries tab refreshes, so
146	// opening the browser reads a file rather than the network — which is what
147	// removed the resolving state D13 is about, rather than papering over it.
148	func newRegistryBrowser(
149		registries []config.RegistryItem,
150		groups map[string]cache.RegistryGroupEntry,
151		deselected map[string]bool,
152		width, height int,
153	) *RegistryBrowser {
154		repoInput := textinput.New()
155		repoInput.Placeholder = "nginx  (or library/nginx)"
156		repoInput.CharLimit = 256
157		theme.StyleTextInput(&repoInput)
158		repoInput.Focus()
159	
160		fi := textinput.New()
161		fi.Placeholder = "filter tags…"
162		fi.CharLimit = 128
163		theme.StyleTextInput(&fi)
164	
165		tagCols := []table.Column{
166			{Title: "Registry", Width: 20},
167			{Title: "Tag", Width: 30},
168			{Title: "Updated", Width: 16},
169			{Title: "C", Width: 4},
170			{Title: "H", Width: 4},
171			{Title: "M", Width: 4},
172			{Title: "L", Width: 4},
173		}
174		tt := table.New(
175			table.WithColumns(tagCols),
176			table.WithFocused(true),
177			table.WithHeight(10),
178		)
179		tt.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
180	
181		sp := spinner.New()
182		sp.Spinner = spinner.Dot
183		sp.Style = theme.SpinnerStyle()
184	
185		b := &RegistryBrowser{
186			registries:   registries,
187			width:        width,
188			height:       height,
189			repoInput:    repoInput,
190			selectedRegs: make(map[string]bool),
191			focusedField: brFieldRepo,
192			filterInput:  fi,
193			tagSortCol:   tagSortByName,
194			tagSortDesc:  false,
195			tagTable:     tt,
196			spinner:      sp,
197			scanCache:    make(map[string]cache.ImageScanEntry),
198			scanningTags: make(map[string]bool),
199			state:        browserStateInput,
200		}
201		b.buildEntries(groups, deselected)
202		b.resizeInputs()
203		b.resizeTagTable()
204		b.updateFocus()
205		return b
206	}
207	
208	// buildEntries expands every configured registry into the lines the picker
209	// shows: a group into its cached members under a header, anything else into
210	// itself.
211	//
212	// A selection is remembered as the entries that were *un*checked, so a member
213	// discovered since the last visit arrives checked like every other new one.
214	func (b *RegistryBrowser) buildEntries(groups map[string]cache.RegistryGroupEntry, deselected map[string]bool) {
215		b.entries = nil
216		b.rows = nil
217		for _, reg := range b.registries {
218			alias := browserAlias(reg)
219			// Members share their group's host and therefore its single credential
220			// entry, so they share the decision the group made about using it.
221			mode := config.ResolveAuthMode(reg, nil)
222	
223			members := groups[reg.Slug].Members
224			if reg.Kind != config.KindGroup || len(members) == 0 {
225				// A group nobody has discovered yet is offered as itself: it is a
226				// pullable registry too, and hiding it would be worse than listing
227				// it without the members it may have.
228				b.rows = append(b.rows, pickerRow{label: alias, entry: len(b.entries)})
229				b.entries = append(b.entries, browserRegistryEntry{
230					URL: reg.URL, Alias: alias, Slug: reg.Slug, authMode: mode,
231					key: reg.Slug,
232				})
233				continue
234			}
235	
236			b.rows = append(b.rows, pickerRow{groupSlug: reg.Slug, label: alias, entry: -1})
237			for _, m := range members {
238				b.rows = append(b.rows, pickerRow{label: "  " + m.Alias, entry: len(b.entries)})
239				b.entries = append(b.entries, browserRegistryEntry{
240					URL:         m.URL,
241					Alias:       m.Alias,
242					Slug:        reg.Slug,
243					ParentAlias: alias,
244					ParentSlug:  reg.Slug,
245					parentURL:   reg.URL,
246					authMode:    mode,
247					key:         memberKey(reg.Slug, m.URL),
248				})
249			}
250		}
251	
252		b.selectedRegs = make(map[string]bool, len(b.entries))
253		for _, e := range b.entries {
254			b.selectedRegs[e.key] = !deselected[e.key]
255		}
256	}
257	
258	// memberKey names one member of a group. Scoping it by the group's slug is what
259	// keeps two groups fronting the same repository apart, and what keeps a member
260	// from colliding with a standalone registry keyed on its own slug.
261	func memberKey(groupSlug, memberURL string) string {
262		return groupSlug + "/" + memberURL
263	}
264	
265	// browserAlias returns what a registry is labelled with in the browser.
266	func browserAlias(reg config.RegistryItem) string {
267		if reg.Alias != "" {
268			return reg.Alias
269		}
270		return reg.URL
271	}
272	
273	// selected reports whether an entry is checked.
274	func (b *RegistryBrowser) selected(e browserRegistryEntry) bool { return b.selectedRegs[e.key] }
275	
276	// groupState reports whether all, none or some of a group's members are checked.
277	func (b *RegistryBrowser) groupState(slug string) theme.CheckState {
278		checked, total := 0, 0
279		for _, e := range b.entries {
280			if e.ParentSlug != slug {
281				continue
282			}
283			total++
284			if b.selected(e) {
285				checked++
286			}
287		}
288		switch {
289		case total == 0 || checked == 0:
290			return theme.CheckNone
291		case checked == total:
292			return theme.CheckAll
293		default:
294			return theme.CheckSome
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// toggleGroup checks every member of a group, or unchecks them when they were
299	// all already checked. A partial selection resolves upwards: the user is more
300	// likely to be completing it than discarding it.
301	func (b *RegistryBrowser) toggleGroup(slug string) {
302		want := b.groupState(slug) != theme.CheckAll
303		for _, e := range b.entries {
304			if e.ParentSlug == slug {
305				b.selectedRegs[e.key] = want
306			}
307		}
308	}
309	
310	// Deselected returns the keys of the entries the user unchecked, which is what
311	// is remembered between visits.
312	func (b *RegistryBrowser) Deselected() []string {
313		var out []string
314		for _, e := range b.entries {
315			if !b.selected(e) {
316				out = append(out, e.key)
317			}
318		}
319		return out
320	}
321	
322	// SetSize updates dimensions and resizes internal components.
323	func (b *RegistryBrowser) SetSize(width, height int) {
324		b.width = width
325		b.height = height
326		b.resizeInputs()
327		b.resizeTagTable()
328	}
329	
330	func (b *RegistryBrowser) resizeInputs() {
331		w := max(b.width-22, 20)
332		b.repoInput.Width = w
333		b.filterInput.Width = max(b.width-6, 10)
334	}
335	
336	func (b *RegistryBrowser) resizeTagTable() {
337		b.tagTable.SetHeight(max(b.height, 1))
338	
339		// b.width is already the viewport content width (full width - 2 borders).
340		// Subtract only the cell padding (numCols × 2) so column widths sum exactly to `available`.
341		const numCols = 7
342		available := max(b.width-numCols*2, 10)
343		fixedReg := 20
344		fixedUpdated := 16
345		fixedC, fixedH, fixedM := 4, 4, 4
346		fixedSum := fixedReg + fixedUpdated + fixedC + fixedH + fixedM
347		flexTag := max(available-fixedSum-4, 8) // reserve 4 for last col minimum
348	
349		cols := b.tagTable.Columns()
350		if len(cols) == numCols {
351			cols[0].Width = fixedReg
352			cols[1].Width = flexTag
353			cols[2].Width = fixedUpdated
354			cols[3].Width = fixedC
355			cols[4].Width = fixedH
356			cols[5].Width = fixedM
357			// Last column absorbs leftover so sum(col_widths) == available exactly.
358			cols[6].Width = available - fixedReg - flexTag - fixedUpdated - fixedC - fixedH - fixedM
359			b.tagTable.SetColumns(cols)
360		}
361	
362		// Force the Selected row style to span the viewport content width so the selected
363		// background extends to the right border, even when row content visually differs
364		// from the calculated width (e.g. Nerd Font icon width discrepancies). See workspaces fix.
365		styles := theme.DefaultTableStyles()
366		styles.Selected = styles.Selected.Width(b.width)
367		b.tagTable.SetStyles(styles)
368	}
